goal: Let a security analyst or admin generate a high-fidelity phishing simulation template in roughly 10 seconds from either a free-text scenario description or an uploaded real email, without depending on a central content team.
constraints: Uploaded .eml and screenshot content must be sandboxed, sanitized, and isolated per workspace
RBAC gates view, edit, and deploy separately
All AI generation and edit actions must be logged for auditability
assumptions: Text-based redaction is sufficient to remove sensitive/org-specific data from a generated template
Difficulty can be changed after generation by re-running the agentic pass on the existing draft
A template library exists as a save destination with no further behavior specified
Copy an Email and Describe a Scenario carry the same permission requirements
gaps: Redaction cannot reach sensitive content embedded in images (logos, signature blocks, addresses baked into graphics)
No stated behavior when difficulty is changed after manual WYSIWYG edits have been made
No retention, deletion, or training-pipeline-exclusion policy for uploaded raw .eml/screenshot content
Template library has no defined list, search, filter, sort, or delete behavior
No mandatory human review/attestation step before deploying a template sourced from a real uploaded email
Phishing category list origin (fixed enum vs. admin-configurable) is unspecified
Audit logging covers actions but not whether prior draft versions are recoverable
edge_cases: Generation fails outright distinct from exceeding the ~10s target
Sanitization strips or rejects part of an upload with no described analyst-facing message
Template library empty state on first use
View-only role opens a template in the editor
Copy an Email permission separate from Describe a Scenario permission
Cross-workspace access attempt on a template ID
Sparse or single-word scenario prompt with no minimum length enforced
Plaintext-only .eml with no layout to preserve
Duplicate template name within a workspace
Template library at scale with no search or filter
Regenerate action distinct from difficulty-triggered re-adjustment, with no overwrite warning
No delete flow described for templates
Editing on mobile/tablet not addressed (preview only is described)
Drag-and-drop block reordering has no keyboard-operable alternative

critical_questions.question: Where are raw .eml uploads and screenshots stored after generation, for how long, and are they excluded from logging or model-training pipelines given they may contain real PII?
If an analyst manually edits a draft and then changes the difficulty setting, does the agentic re-adjustment pass preserve, merge with, or overwrite those edits?
Should Copy an Email require a distinct or higher permission tier than Describe a Scenario, given it ingests real third-party content rather than a text prompt?
What are the actual success metrics for this feature — adoption, time saved versus the prior content-team workflow, or percentage of AI drafts deployed with no manual edits?
Can sensitive-data redaction reach content embedded in images, and if not, what's the fallback — strip inline images by default, or flag for mandatory manual review?
Is there a delete flow for templates, and what happens on the campaign launcher side if a linked template is deleted or edited?
Should deploying a template generated from a real uploaded email require an explicit human attestation step beyond generic RBAC deploy permission?
Is the phishing category list a fixed enum or admin-configurable/extensible with custom values?

design_risks: Silent edit loss if difficulty re-adjustment overwrites manual WYSIWYG edits with no warning or undo path
Redaction blind spot on sensitive content embedded in images, undermining the core 'sensitive data replaced with placeholders' claim
Unscoped raw-content ingestion via Copy an Email creates a compliance liability with no stated retention limit or review gate
Underspecified template library risks either late scope growth in eng estimation or an unusable flat list at moderate volume
teaching_notes: knowledge/features/aep-library/ is the closest existing precedent: AI-generated artifact created via guided setup, refined in a Test & Refine step, backed by a filterable library table with status flow, search, row actions, and an empty state — model this feature's library on it directly
Apply the 'errors inform, don't punish' principle to generation failures and sanitization rejections: tell the analyst specifically what was flagged and why
Trust & Safety principle applies directly: this feature claims to redact sensitive data and produce safe links, so any gap between that claim and actual behavior is a trust failure, not just a bug
Apply Visibility of System Status (heuristics.md #1) to the ~10s generation window and to sanitization — show progress, never a silent wait
